rooms.heading:
Rooms built for
{{one subject each.}}
body: Sunbeam’s STEM provision is a set of named rooms rather than a claim about a culture. Physics, Chemistry and Biology each have a laboratory of their own, carrying {' '}**board practicals from Class IX to Class XII** — a chemistry bench with gas taps and reagent shelves is a different object from a science room with a sink in it.

The **mathematics laboratory** is the one most schools do without. Its purpose is to make mathematics a practical subject — something handled rather than only argued on paper — which is a harder room to justify and a more revealing one to have.

bots.heading:
Four things
{{in one room.}}
body: The school’s description of its Robotics Lab is a single line of four items, and it is more specific than most schools manage: **a drone, a 3-D printer, a telescope and embedded systems**. No “state-of-the-art”, no “cutting-edge” — four objects, each of which either exists in a room or does not.
bots.caption: The school has published no photograph of this laboratory, so the four items are set as type rather than illustrated with somebody else’s room.

use.heading:
Not just equipment.
{{Students using it.}}
body: Laboratories are only useful when they are in use. Six frames from the school’s own rooms — each caption says what is actually in the picture.

eco.heading:
Many rooms.
{{One purpose.}}
body: Different spaces, different tools. One connected idea of learning through doing.
Out of the Robotics Lab: **second place at the RoboWunder International Robotics Championship, Kuala Lumpur**. The rest is on {' '}Student Success.

close.heading:
Explore. Build.
{{Discover.}}
body: The school names the rooms, their contents and the programmes it enters. It does not publish a coding curriculum, which classes take robotics, or club hours — and it has published no photograph of the Robotics Lab itself.
